fields.m.setting: Middle-school ESE resource room and general education electives; 1:1 para for electives
fields.m.beh: Grabbing and property aggression: taking an item from another person's hands or desk, throwing or sweeping items off a surface, or pushing a person while reaching for an item. Not: picking up an unattended item.
fields.m.eadesign: multielement with a tangible condition, 4 series (EA-1, 9/8–9/12)
fields.m.reinf: Access to the iPad and to peers' fidget items; EO strongest at the end of a preferred activity and when a peer has an item.
fields.m.prec: Repeats the item's name ('iPad, iPad'), reaches toward it, stands up.
fields.m.repdesc: Says 'iPad please' when the item is in view and an adult prompts; does not accept 'wait' or 'later'.
fields.m.pref: PA-1 (MSWO, 9/5): iPad (video) > handheld game > fidget cube > music.
fields.m.curr: Electives are appropriate; resource-room work is at his level.
fields.m.constraints: Shared iPads in the resource room; electives have 25 peers.
fields.m.safety: A peer was scratched once; items broken twice this month.
fields.sel.why: From the model's questions; see the rationale on each card.
fields.cp[0].s0: Set the initial delivery interval below the mean baseline interresponse time (dense; near-continuous for severe behavior; Hagopian et al., 1994).
fields.cp[0].s1: Deliver the reinforcer (attention or the item) at each interval end regardless of behavior; keep the delivery brief and consistent.
fields.cp[0].s2: Withhold the reinforcer contingent on problem behavior (extinction) where feasible; delay a scheduled delivery briefly if problem behavior immediately precedes it.
fields.cp[0].s3: Thin the interval by steps when the criterion is met, toward a terminal schedule the setting can sustain.
fields.cp[0].s4: Introduce FCT after thinning rather than during a rich NCR schedule (Goh et al., 2000).
fields.cp[1].s0: Match the form to the function: escape → continue the task through the prompt sequence with guided compliance and do not remove the demand; attention → no attention, comments, or eye contact contingent on the behavior; tangible → the item is not returned contingent on the behavior.
fields.cp[1].s1: Specify what implementers do during the behavior (block per the safety plan only; blocking is a consequence and must be neutral).
fields.cp[1].s2: Prepare implementers for a possible burst or aggression early in treatment and for the slower onset of effect; pair extinction with a reinforcement component whenever possible.
fields.cp[1].s3: Score every session for reinforcement errors: any instance in which the behavior contacted the reinforcer.
fields.cp[1].s4: Review integrity weekly; low integrity risks intermittent reinforcement and greater resistance to extinction (McConnachie & Carr, 1997, as reviewed by Geiger et al., 2010).
fields.cp[2].s0: Before the routine in which the behavior occurs, provide free access to the maintaining reinforcer (attention or the item) for a set period.
fields.cp[2].s1: Begin the routine immediately after; expect lower value of the reinforcer and less behavior for a limited window.
fields.cp[2].s2: Record the length of the effect and adjust timing; combine with the consequence components rather than relying on it alone.
fields.cp[3].s0: Provide a visual or picture activity schedule the student manipulates (check off, move a card) as each activity ends.
fields.cp[3].s1: Give an advance notice before transitions (e.g., 2-min and 30-s warnings) and a consistent transition signal.
fields.cp[3].s2: Preview any change to the routine at the start of the day; keep the order stable where possible.
fields.cp[3].s3: For transition-evoked behavior, combine with the function-based component identified on EA-1 (Wilder et al., 2006).
fields.cp[4].s0: Preview the next day's or next period's materials in a low-demand, preferred context (with a parent or aide) before the lesson.
fields.cp[4].s1: Keep priming brief and reinforcing; do not test.
fields.cp[4].s2: Track performance and problem behavior in the primed lessons versus unprimed ones.
fields.cp[5].s0: Identify from the SP-1 and ABC-1 data which peers, locations, and materials precede the behavior.
fields.cp[5].s1: Seat the student away from evocative peers and doorways (or near the exit route when elopement is the target and a staff member sits between), with materials within reach and the break area visible.
fields.cp[5].s2: Use row seating for independent work; rearrange only after data show a problem with the current arrangement.
fields.cp[5].s3: Review the arrangement at each plan review.
fields.cp[6].s0: Assess preference with the method chosen in part B; separate leisure from edible classes.
fields.cp[6].s1: Set access duration to match the treatment context (Steinhilber & Johnson, 2007); use accumulated access for activities that lose value when interrupted.
fields.cp[6].s2: Validate with a reinforcer assessment; rotate items and offer choice.
fields.cp[7].s0: Completing a unit schedule (e.g., FR 3 correct) earns a token; completing the exchange schedule (e.g., 5 tokens) earns the backup reinforcer.
fields.cp[7].s1: Establish tokens by pairing with immediate exchange at first (exchange after 1 token), then lengthen the exchange requirement.
fields.cp[7].s2: Offer a menu of backup reinforcers to limit satiation; keep the exchange schedule dense enough to contact the backup daily.
fields.cp[7].s3: Thin the unit schedule before the exchange schedule.
fields.cp[8].s0: Place items in a circle; allow 5 min of free engagement with no items removed; record engagement in 10-s partial intervals.
fields.cp[8].s1: Rank by percentage of intervals engaged; use for students whose problem behavior is evoked by item removal.
fields.cp[8].s2: Follow with a concurrent-schedule reinforcer assessment.
fields.cp[9].s0: Arrange two or more component schedules, each in effect during a distinct signal (e.g., red card = mands reinforced; white card = mands not reinforced).
fields.cp[9].s1: Begin with the reinforcement component in effect most of the time (e.g., 80%) and lengthen the extinction component gradually.
fields.cp[9].s2: Provide alternative reinforcers during the extinction component (Hagopian et al., 2011).
fields.cp[9].s3: Teach the discrimination: reinforce only during the signal; never reinforce during the other signal.
fields.cp[9].s4: Relapse note: the SΔ from a signaled multiple schedule also mitigates resurgence when it is present during an extinction challenge — a mean 81% reduction in Fisher et al. (2020); see Form RM-1.
fields.cp[10].s0: Reinforce after a number of responses that varies around a mean (e.g., VR 5: 3, 7, 5, 4, 6).
fields.cp[10].s1: Prepare the sequence in advance so staff follow it rather than deciding in the moment.
fields.cp[10].s2: Use for steady, high-rate responding without post-reinforcement pauses; thin the mean gradually.
fields.cp[11].s0: Reinforce after a fixed number of responses (e.g., FR 4: every fourth correct).
fields.cp[11].s1: Raise the ratio in small steps only when responding is stable; expect a pause after each reinforcer.
fields.cp[11].s2: Watch for ratio strain (long pauses, problem behavior) and step back.
fields.cp[12].s0: Begin with the prompt that guarantees the response (e.g., full physical), delivered immediately with the instruction.
fields.cp[12].s1: Reduce to the next less intrusive level after the criterion (e.g., 3 consecutive correct); return one level after 2 errors.
fields.cp[12].s2: Reinforce prompted responses during acquisition; differentially reinforce unprompted responses once they appear.
fields.cp[12].s3: Use when errors evoke problem behavior or the response is new.
fields.cp[13].s0: Begin with a 0-s delay between instruction and prompt; increase the delay in small steps (e.g., 1 s per session or per criterion) as unprompted responses appear.
fields.cp[13].s1: Transfer of control is shown when the learner responds before the prompt; keep the terminal delay short enough to prevent errors.
fields.cp[13].s2: Reinforce unprompted responses more richly than prompted ones.
fields.cp[14].s0: In every teaching trial deliver the instruction and the controlling prompt together (0-s delay).
fields.cp[14].s1: Run daily probe trials without the prompt to measure acquisition; probes are the only unprompted opportunities.
fields.cp[14].s2: Use when errors must be near zero and probes can be scheduled.
fields.cp[15].s0: Compare candidate prompt types (vocal, model, physical) or hierarchies (MTL vs LTM) on equivalent skill sets in an alternating-treatments design.
fields.cp[15].s1: Select the procedure that produced the fastest acquisition with the fewest errors and least problem behavior.
fields.cp[15].s2: Re-run when a new response class is introduced.
fields.cp[16].s0: After an error, model or deliver the correct response, then re-present the instruction and require an independent (or least-prompted) correct response before moving on.
fields.cp[16].s1: Reinforce the corrected response with praise only; reserve the token or item for unprompted responses.
fields.cp[17].s0: Begin with the FCR honored immediately; introduce a signaled delay of a few seconds, then lengthen it stepwise (e.g., 5 → 15 → 30 → 60 s → several minutes) as problem behavior stays low.
fields.cp[17].s1: During the delay, prompt and reinforce engagement in an alternative activity or work (the delay is filled, not empty).
fields.cp[17].s2: Add unpredictable denials with the tolerance response once delays are tolerated.
fields.cp[17].s3: Step back one level after two sessions with problem behavior during the delay.
fields.cp[18].s0: Select the mand: recognizable to novel listeners, quickly acquired, less effortful than the problem behavior; a card or switch may precede a vocal form (Tiger et al., 2008).
fields.cp[18].s1: Start in a controlled setting with a trained implementer; contrive the establishing operation (present the demand / divert attention / remove the item) several times per session.
fields.cp[18].s2: Prompt the mand at the EO: most-to-least (physical prompt immediately, faded across trials; Fisher et al., 1993) or least-to-most with a 5-s progressive delay (Shirley et al., 1997).
fields.cp[18].s3: Reinforce every mand with the functional reinforcer immediately (CRF); a break of 1 min, 20–30 s of attention, or the item.
fields.cp[18].s4: Withhold the reinforcer for the problem behavior (extinction); if problem behavior occurs with the mand, do not reinforce and re-present the EO (Harding et al., 2009).
fields.cp[18].s5: For escape: chain a work requirement before the mand opportunity and raise it as behavior improves (Lalli et al., 1995; Harding et al., 2009).
fields.cp[18].s6: Thin with a signaled multiple schedule (reinforcement and extinction periods with distinct cues; Hanley et al., 2001) or a signaled delay faded from 1 s toward 30 s (Fisher et al., 2000); provide alternative reinforcers during extinction periods (Hagopian et al., 2011).
fields.cp[18].s7: Add trainers and settings, include common stimuli, and probe untrained contexts; increase response complexity after acquisition.
fields.cp[19].s0: Assess: offer a choice between a small immediate reinforcer and a larger delayed one; record the baseline choice.
fields.cp[19].s1: Begin with the larger reinforcer at no delay so the student chooses it; then add a short delay to the larger option and increase it gradually across sessions.
fields.cp[19].s2: Provide an intervening activity (a task or leisure item) during the delay; choosing the larger delayed option with the activity increased tolerance (Dixon et al., 2003).
fields.cp[19].s3: Continue until the student reliably chooses the larger delayed reinforcer at the terminal delay; probe in the natural routine.
fields.cp[20].s0: After the tolerance response, present one contextually appropriate behavior (relinquish the item, transition, or complete one instruction) before the synthesized reinforcers are delivered.
fields.cp[20].s1: Lengthen the chain and vary its content unpredictably (one instruction → three → a short task → a full routine) while keeping some trials in which the FCR is honored immediately.
fields.cp[20].s2: Reinforce the chain with the synthesized reinforcers at a decreasing but unpredictable probability; add praise throughout.
fields.cp[20].s3: Extend to new implementers and settings with the same sequence; probe the natural routine before and after.
fields.cp[21].s0: Assess the current mand: does it occur only after a vocal prompt or the item in view (prompt or stimulus control) or under the EO alone?
fields.cp[21].s1: Fade the prompt and the visible item with a time delay so the mand occurs in the absence of both.
fields.cp[21].s2: For sign or picture mands, pair the vocal model and reinforce vocal approximations to move toward vocal mands (Carbone et al., 2010).
fields.cp[22].s0: Capture naturally occurring EOs during routines (snack, play, transitions); pause and wait for the mand before providing the item or action.
fields.cp[22].s1: Prompt only as needed, fade quickly, and reinforce with the item requested.
fields.cp[22].s2: Rotate across settings, listeners, and items to build generalized manding; record mands per hour in the natural routine.
fields.cp[23].s0: Before the activity, have the student state what they will do ("I will use the break card if the work is hard"); reinforce the statement at first (reinforce-saying phase).
fields.cp[23].s1: Shift reinforcement to correspondence: reinforce only when the stated behavior occurs (reinforce-correspondence phase); use say-then-do ordering (Israel & O'Leary, 1973).
fields.cp[23].s2: Fade to intermittent checks and to the student's own review of correspondence.
fields.cp[23].s3: Use when the student can state a plan and the goal is self-management across settings.
fields.cp[24].s0: Assess the must-have skills first: requesting, waiting after requests, accepting removals and transitions, completing brief tasks, accepting "no," and health and safety routines.
fields.cp[24].s1: Select the alternative method of speaking (vocal, sign, picture, device) from the student's repertoire and teach requests first.
fields.cp[24].s2: Sequence the remaining must-have skills alongside the reduction plan; record the level of prompting and the settings in which each skill occurs.
fields.cp[25].p0: Block the grab (body between him and the item); the item is not delivered after a grab; keep the item out of reach; prompt the request at the next quiet moment and honor it after the wait.
fields.cp[25].p2: If a peer is injured, CR-1; items thrown: clear the area, no restraint.
fields.cp[25].s0: On the precursor: At "iPad, iPad" or the reach: prompt "iPad please" or the card; honor it if the item is available; if not, signal the wait with the timer card and start the delay.
fields.cp[25].s1: On the target behavior: Block the grab (body between him and the item); the item is not delivered after a grab; keep the item out of reach; prompt the request at the next quiet moment and honor it after the wait.
fields.cp[25].s2: After the episode: Return the item to its place; continue the activity; record the episode and the item on DD-1.
fields.cp[25].s3: Staff do not: Do not give the item after a grab "to calm him"; do not take the iPad away for the day as a punishment; do not argue.
fields.cp[25].s4: Record the episode, the step used, and whether the reinforcer was contacted (integrity error).
fields.cp[25].s5: Crisis procedure applies only when the safety trigger is met and is documented separately.
fields.cp[26].bsrc: Progressive delay fading on a variable-interval schedule after FCT for elopement (Stevenson et al., 2016)
fields.cp[26].p0: VI 15 s, 30 s, 45 s, 90 s, then 300 s; advance after 3 consecutive sessions with no elopement, using preset interval lists (e.g., VI 30 s drew from 5, 10, 15, 30, 35, 40, 45 and 60 s)
fields.cp[26].p2: the adult tells the student the item will have to wait and invites them to keep walking
fields.cp[26].s0: Start delay fading only after FCT has produced steady requests and rare elopement.
fields.cp[26].s1: When the student requests an item or activity, tell the student it has to wait and keep walking together; start the interval timer at that moment.
fields.cp[26].s2: Praise calm walking near the adult while the interval runs.
fields.cp[26].s3: When the interval has ended, give the item or activity for the student's next appropriate request.
fields.cp[26].s4: If the requested item is not available at all, say it is not possible right now and suggest looking for something else on the walk.
fields.cp[26].s5: Draw each interval from the preset list for the current VI value so the wait is unpredictable.
fields.cp[26].s6: Advance to the next VI value (15, 30, 45, 90, then 300 s) after 3 consecutive sessions without elopement.
fields.cp[26].data: Elopements and appropriate requests per 10-min walk, plus the VI value in effect, recorded on Form DD-1.
fields.cp[26].mat: Timer or phone app with preset interval lists for each VI value, data sheet.
fields.cp[27].bsrc: Functional communication training with extinction and gradual, signaled schedule thinning (practice guide) (Tiger et al., 2008)
fields.cp[27].p0: a low-effort response that unfamiliar people will recognize and the student can learn fast, such as a picture exchange, a single sign, a voice-output button or a short vocal request; an existing response such as signing 'all done' can be strengthened; make it more complex once problem behavior is low
fields.cp[27].p1: most-to-least (physical prompt as soon as the motivating situation is set up, then faded in intensity) or least-to-most with a delay (wait about 5 s, then a vocal or physical prompt, with the delay lengthened over trials)
fields.cp[27].p2: the reinforcer found in the functional analysis, given every time at first; if extinction cannot be used, make reinforcement for the communication longer, better, faster or more frequent than for problem behavior
fields.cp[27].p3: withhold the maintaining reinforcer after problem behavior from the start of treatment
fields.cp[27].p4: lengthen a delay to reinforcement starting at 1 s with a signal that it is coming; or alternate signaled periods when requests are and are not honored (for example two colored cards); for escape, raise the amount of work required before a break request is honored
fields.cp[27].p5: a schedule caregivers can keep up; the guide cites success with requests honored only during signaled periods covering about 20% of the time
fields.cp[27].s0: Confirm the maintaining reinforcer with a functional analysis before starting.
fields.cp[27].s1: Pick a communication response that is low effort, easy for unfamiliar people to recognize, and quick to learn.
fields.cp[27].s2: Begin with a trained interventionist in a safe, controlled setting and create many practice opportunities by setting up the motivating situation (remove the item, withhold attention, or present the task).
fields.cp[27].s3: Prompt the communication response either right away (most-to-least) or after a short wait such as 5 s (least-to-most with a delay), and fade the prompt over trials.
fields.cp[27].s4: Deliver the maintaining reinforcer every time the student communicates during initial training.
fields.cp[27].s5: Withhold the maintaining reinforcer after problem behavior.
fields.cp[27].s6: Once problem behavior is low, thin reinforcement gradually using a signaled delay starting at 1 s, signaled periods when requests can and cannot be honored, or, for escape, more work before the break request is honored.
fields.cp[27].s7: Offer other preferred items during delays or unavailable periods to compete with problem behavior during thinning.
fields.cp[27].s8: Extend training across several trainers and settings, bring in materials from the classroom, train in each needed setting, and teach caregivers how to respond.
fields.cp[27].s9: Increase the complexity of the communication response over time, for example a full request such as 'May I have ___, please'.
fields.cp[27].data: Rate of problem behavior and of independent communication responses per session, prompt level used, and the current thinning step, plus probes in each setting and with each caregiver, recorded on Form DD-1.
fields.cp[27].mat: Communication materials (picture cards, voice-output device or sign), the reinforcer identified in the functional analysis, signals for reinforcement availability such as colored cards, a timer, and a protected setting for early training.
fields.sch.0: maintenance and thinning of an acquired response
fields.sch.chosen: TANG, S_SO, PA_FO, S_MULT, S_VR, S_FR
fields.ec.0: no, the prompting procedure is errorless
fields.skb.1: contrived sessions first, then natural routines
fields.sk.chosen: DT_PROG, FCT, SC_TRAIN, SBT_CAB, MAND_XFER, MAND_NET, SAYDO, EFL
fields.rb.prec: At "iPad, iPad" or the reach: prompt "iPad please" or the card; honor it if the item is available; if not, signal the wait with the timer card and start the delay.
fields.rb.target: Block the grab (body between him and the item); the item is not delivered after a grab; keep the item out of reach; prompt the request at the next quiet moment and honor it after the wait.
fields.rb.after: Return the item to its place; continue the activity; record the episode and the item on DD-1.
fields.rb.not: Do not give the item after a grab "to calm him"; do not take the iPad away for the day as a punishment; do not argue.
fields.rb.crisis: If a peer is injured, CR-1; items thrown: clear the area, no restraint.
fields.p.visit: Weekly 30-minute visit: observe one session, score the integrity checklist, give feedback, model any step under 80%.
fields.p.pre: Probes before the plan starts: the target and the replacement behavior in 3 settings (class, specials, cafeteria) with 2 adults.
fields.p.gen: Train with two adults and in two settings from the first week; the natural cue (the demand itself) is the SD; the card goes with the student.
fields.p.post: Probes in the untrained setting at 2 and 4 weeks after criterion; monthly after.
fields.p.complex: The simple response first; the longer form once the simple one is at criterion.
fields.p.design: Baseline to treatment with the EA-1 treatment sheet; reversal only if the team agrees.
